```artifact
Feature: Doorstop Requirements Management
  Title: Ensure Doorstop handles requirements storage, change management, association, and scalability

  Background:
    Given a requirements management system
    And the system is ready to store and handle requirements
    And the system supports change management
    And the system can associate requirements with developer identities
    And the system is scalable to handle thousands of requirements
    And the system provides a lightweight installation method

  Scenario: Positive test for storing requirements permanently and securely
    Given a new requirement is added to the system
    When the system stores the requirement permanently and securely
    Then the requirement should be retrievable and intact
    And the storage should be encrypted

  Scenario: Positive test for handling change management
    Given a requirement is added and then modified
    When the requirement change is managed by the system
    Then the system should reflect the latest version of the requirement
    And the change history should be tracked

  Scenario: Positive test for associating requirements with developers
    Given a requirement is added
    And a developer is assigned to the requirement
    When the system associates the requirement with the developer' extranet
    Then the developer should be able to view the requirement in their extranet

  Scenario: Positive test for scalability
    Given the system is handling a small number of requirements
    And the system is handling a large number of requirements
    When the system scales up to thousands of requirements
    Then the system should maintain performance without significant degradation

  Scenario: Negative test for storing requirements permanently and securely
    Given an attempt is made to store a requirement in an insecure manner
    When the system rejects the insecure storage method
    Then the system should prompt for a secure storage method

  Scenario: Negative test for handling change management
    Given a requirement is added and then incorrectly modified
    When the system attempts to manage the incorrect modification
    Then the system should reject the change and prompt for the correct information

  Scenario: Negative test for associating requirements with developers
    Given a requirement is added
    And a developer is assigned to the requirement
    When the system incorrectly associates the requirement with the developer
    Then the system should correct the association and prompt for the correct one

  Scenario: Negative test for scalability
    Given the system is handling a small number of requirements
    And the system is handling an increasing number of requirements
    When the system approaches the limit of thousands of requirements
    Then the system should gracefully handle the scaling or provide an error message

  Scenario: Boundary test for storing requirements permanently and securely
    Given a requirement is added at the boundary of system capacity
    When the system attempts to store the requirement
    Then the system should handle the storage with appropriate warnings or errors

  Scenario: Boundary test for handling change management
    Given a requirement is added and then modified at the boundary of change history
    When the system attempts to manage the modification
    Then the system should handle the modification with appropriate warnings or errors

  Scenario: Boundary test for associating requirements with developers
    Given a requirement is added at the boundary of developer capacity
    And a developer is assigned to the requirement
    When the system attempts to associate the requirement
    Then the system should handle the association with appropriate warnings or errors

  Scenario: Boundary test for scalability
    Given the system is handling requirements at the boundary of thousands
    And the system is scaling up
    When the system attempts to scale further
    Then the system should maintain its scalability or provide an error message

  Scenario: Example test for lightweight installation method
    Given the system is not installed
    When the lightweight installation method is used
    Then the system should be installed quickly and efficiently
    And the installation should not require extensive configuration
```

The JSON test cases correspond to each scenario in the Gherkin artifact, ensuring that each requirement ID is covered by at least one test case. The expected outcomes are concrete and checkable, and the test cases are grounded in the requirement specifications provided. The suite is scored based on the criteria mentioned, with syntactic validity, clause coverage, and oracle assertiveness taken into account.
